lens: Lens 1 — the concentration function and the gates: (i) kink density as the h->0 small-ball limit and what the closure gets wrong at the kink; (ii) C12/C11 specialised to the commutative algebra L^inf(R^n, N(0,I)): sensitivity law, exponent, and the (1+tau)^{-1/2} profile on Eldan's path; (iii) inverse Littlewood-Offord / LCD for Gaussian rows times a structured previous layer. Scripts and logs: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-thehonesttorus-github-io/9523ef6a-ff73-5ab2-8be3-275df2b5fcc6/scratchpad/wf/lens1/ (edgeworth_split2.py, injected_test.py, eldan_kink.py -> eldan_kink.log, skew_collective.py -> .log, skew_rank.py -> .log, identities.py, a_integral.py). All numerics on official net 0 (W_off0.npy, mccache_0.npz with S=2^20, chaindump_0.npz, truth_off0.npz), float64, OMP_NUM_THREADS=2.

claims.claim: C1 (i). The chain's kink density phi(alpha_a)/sigma_a is the Gaussian surrogate's value of f_a(0) = lim_{h->0} P(|z_a| <= h)/(2h), and the limit exists for the true law: the pre-activation law is absolutely continuous with a continuous density, small-ball exponent exactly 1 (Q_a(t) := P(|z_a|<=t) = 2 f_a(0) t + O(t^2)), no atom at the kink.
claims.argument: Structure: the network is piecewise linear on the finitely many gate cones C_g = {x : gates(x) = g}; on C_g, z_a = <t_a(g), x> with t_a(g) = row a of W_l D(g_{l-1}) ... D(g_1) W_1, and x ~ N(0,I) restricted to C_g. For every g whose cone has positive Gaussian measure, t_a(g) is a non-identically-zero polynomial of the Gaussian weights, hence nonzero a.s.; the law of a nonzero linear functional of a cone-truncated Gaussian has a continuous density (a Gaussian section measure of a convex polyhedral cone, continuous in the level, with at most a corner at level 0). A finite mixture of such laws is absolutely continuous with continuous density, so Q_a(t)/(2t) -> f_a(0) and Q_a(t) = 2 f_a(0) t + O(t^2). For the Gaussian surrogate N(m,sigma^2): Phi(h/sigma - alpha) - Phi(-h/sigma - alpha) = 2h phi(alpha)/sigma (1 + O(h^2/sigma^2)), so f^G(0) = phi(alpha)/sigma. Value: the our-data reader's Q_l(h)/G_l(h) = 1.000-1.003 at h = 0.003..0.1 sigma for all 16 layers (N = 262144; layer 0, exactly Gaussian, gives 0.9994-1.0004 as calibration), i.e. the true small-ball mass at the kink equals the Gaussian value with the true (m, sigma) to 1e-3-3e-3, and the excess equals the Edgeworth (g3, g4) prediction (1.0007-1.0027). My own pass (eldan_kink.py, N = 32768, window 0.1 sigma) reproduces this: the empirical f(0) and phi(alpha)/sigma agree to 0.2% in the neuron mean at layers 2, 6, 10, 14 (Table B3 columns /emp vs /Gauss).
claims.consequence_for_system: The kink density that enters the births (w_a = phi(alpha_a)/sigma_a) and the sensitivity law is the correct physical quantity, and its Gaussian value is right to 3e-3 when (m, sigma) are right. Therefore closure errors at the kink are errors in (m, sigma) (first-order lever) and in the density's derivatives (C3), not in the small-ball mass; no Littlewood-Offord-type correction to the mass (additive e^{-cn} terms, lattice excess) exists. The lim h->0 identification also says the concentration-function viewpoint adds nothing beyond f_a(0) for a continuous law.
claims.test: Already decisive: the reader's N = 262144 ratio table at h = 0.003 sigma. A sharper test of 'no atom / exponent 1' is the ratio Q(h)/Q(h/10) = 10.00 +- Poisson at h = 0.01 sigma (reader's table gives 1.0011/0.9994 against the Gaussian at both scales, consistent).

claims.claim: C2 (i)+(ii). Sensitivity law with the TRUE density: for any neuron, if dz = sqrt(eps) sigma xi' with xi' symmetric, independent, E xi'^2 = 1, then E relu(z + dz) - E relu(z) = (1/2) eps sigma^2 f(0) + O(eps^2); and E relu(z+u) - E relu(z) - u P(z>0) = (1/2) u^2 f(0) + O(u^3). So the kink density is the Hessian of the mean readout in the mean direction and twice its derivative in the variance direction; F6's dm = (1/2) eps sigma phi(alpha) is the Gaussian-surrogate case.
claims.argument: Pathwise, (z+d)_+ - z_+ - d 1_{z>0} = int_0^d (d-s) delta_0(z+s) ds, so for fixed d: E[...] = int_0^d (d-s) f(-s) ds = d^2 f(0)/2 - d^3 f'(0)/6 + ...; averaging over d = sqrt(eps) sigma xi' kills the odd term and gives (1/2) eps sigma^2 f(0) + O(eps^2 f''). The mean-shift statement is the same identity with d = u. The Gaussian surrogate gives f(0) = phi(alpha)/sigma, i.e. (1/2) eps sigma phi(alpha) (Prop. sens of sec_central). CHECKED on net 0 (eldan_kink.py Table B3, antithetic injection at layers 2, 6, 10, 14, eps = 1e-3, 1e-2, 1e-1): <dm>/<(1/2) eps sigma^2 f_emp(0)> = 0.997-1.000 at eps <= 1e-2 (0.987-0.999 at eps = 0.1, the O(eps^2) term), per-neuron correlation 0.989-0.999, per-neuron slope 0.9975-1.0008; exponent d log<dm>/d log eps = 0.997, 0.999, 0.999, 1.000. Synthetic check on a non-Gaussian mixture (identities.py): ratio 0.9997 at eps = 1e-3; mean-shift identity ratio 0.992 at u = 0.1.
claims.consequence_for_system: F6 holds with the true density and is exact to 0.3% at eps = 1e-2: a relative variance error eps_a in the chain moves neuron a's mean by (1/2) eps_a sigma_a phi(alpha_a), with lever <sigma phi/2> = 0.28 (layer 0) falling to 0.021 (layer 15) in post-activation units (edgeworth_split2.py Table 1). The Euler-Stein defect's kink content is this Hessian: it is first order in f(0), which is what makes the Gaussian closure's defect decay like one birth (C6).
claims.test: Done (Table B3). The cheapest further check is the same antithetic injection with per-neuron eps_a equal to the chain's own variance error, which should reproduce the chain's injected error up to the truth-noise floor 2.7e-5 (see C4).

claims.claim: C3 (i). The closure's one-step mean error at EXACT (m, sigma) is not the kink mass but the kappa_3-weighted slope (and kappa_4-weighted curvature) of the surrogate density at the kink: E_true relu(z) - sigma d_0(alpha) = -kappa_3 f_G'(0)/6 + kappa_4 f_G''(0)/24 + ..., with f_G'(0) = alpha phi(alpha)/sigma^2, f_G''(0) = (alpha^2-1) phi(alpha)/sigma^3 (this is eq. mean-readout of sec_transport). Per layer the kappa_3 term is 3.5e-4 -> 5.7e-4 rms and the kappa_4 term 1.5e-4 -> 2.0e-4 rms over neurons.
claims.argument: Gram-Charlier: E_nu g = E_G g + sum_{k>=3} kappa_k E_G g^{(k)}/k! to first order in the cumulants; relu'' = delta_0, relu''' = delta_0', relu'''' = delta_0'', and E_G delta_0^{(j)}(z) = (-1)^j f_G^{(j)}(0). Equivalently, by integrating phi He_3 = -phi''' twice against (alpha + x)_+, one gets -alpha phi(alpha): the mean error is -g3 alpha phi sigma/6 + g4 (alpha^2 - 1) phi sigma/24. CHECKED against the 1e9-sample truth with the 2^20-sample (m, sigma, g3, g4) (edgeworth_split2.py Table 1b): the direct residual truth - sigma d_0(alpha) has rms 4.9e-4 - 7.9e-4 (cache noise floor sigma/sqrt(S) = 4.0e-4 - 1.1e-3), its regression slope on the Edgeworth prediction is 0.914-0.934 at layers 3-15 with correlation 0.48 -> 0.81 rising as the floor falls; the sign is right at every layer. Synthetic check on a mixture with g3 = 0.44 (identities.py) gives the right sign and shows the k3+k4 truncation overshoots there (-2.08e-2 vs -1.89e-2), so the formula is a first-order statement valid at our g3 ~ 0.1, not a convergent series.
claims.consequence_for_system: The Gaussian closure's injected error per layer (5-6e-4 rms, the number behind its 4e-6 MSE) is the first-derivative-of-density functional times kappa_3/6; the kappa_3 chain removes it at first order, leaving an injected error 10x smaller (C4). The quantity at the kink that matters is f_G'(0) weighted by the realization-specific kappa_3(z_a) = sum_{ijk} w_ai w_aj w_ak kappa_3(h_i,h_j,h_k), i.e. the hub readout of F1; the kink mass f(0) itself enters only as a propagation coefficient.
claims.test: Done. To push the direct check below the cache floor: recompute (m, sigma, g3, g4) from 1e8 fresh inputs (floor 4e-5) and redo Table 1b; the slope should be 1.00 +- 0.03 at layers 7-15 if the Edgeworth form is complete at this order.

claims.claim: C4 (i). The hypothesis 'the kink mass is the dominant closure error' is false for both chains. The organisers' chain's per-layer error budget on net 0 (chaindump_0): total rms 2.7e-5 (layer 0, = truth-MC floor) -> 1.22e-4 (layer 15); at depth 85% of it is the propagated mean error Phi(alpha) W_l (out_{l-1} - truth_{l-1}) (corr 0.88, slope 0.85 at layer 15; corr 0.58 at layer 8); the injected one-step error is 1.4e-5 -> 5.6e-5 rms, uncorrelated with the full kappa_3 term (|corr| < 0.1, so there is no uniform 10% deficit of the kappa_3 readout) and with the per-neuron kappa_4 fluctuation term (corr -0.03 to -0.17), but correlated with the F6 variance lever (corr 0.2 at layer 7 -> 0.51 at layer 15 despite the cache's 1.4e-3 variance noise). The chain's relative variance error, noise-corrected, is ~0 at layer 0 and ~1.9e-3 at layer 15; times the lever 0.021 this is 4e-5, matching the injected 5.6e-5 after removing the 2.7e-5 truth floor. The true law's kink-mass deviation from the surrogate (1-3e-3 relative) enters the mean only at second order (eps x 3e-3 ~ 1e-6 per layer).
claims.argument: edgeworth_split2.py Tables 1-2 and injected_test.py Table 3. Chain pre-activation mean = W_l out_{l-1} exactly (kprop3 linear step), so dmu is exact; the chaindump 'var' field is the chain's pre-activation variance (verified: var/v_cache - 1 has rms 1.43e-3 at layer 0 where the chain is exact and the cache noise is sqrt(2/S) = 1.38e-3). Regressions over the 1024 neurons per layer. Kink-weighted rms relative error of the chain's own kink density phi(alpha_c)/sigma_c vs the true-moment Gaussian: 5.4e-4 (layer 1) -> 1.4e-3 (layer 15), kink-weighted mean -2e-5 to -1.3e-4: a 1e-3 relative error of the propagation coefficient is a second-order effect. Caveat: chaindump_0 has final MSE 1.5e-8, not the 3.53e-8 quoted in sec_measure (a later configuration of the chain, presumably); the budget shape, not the absolute level, is the claim.
claims.consequence_for_system: What is wrong at the kink in the exact first-order chain is (a) the diagonal of the covariance (variance) at the 2e-3 level at depth, acting through the F6 lever, and (b) the accumulated mean error carried forward with coefficient Phi(alpha) ~ 0.5 per layer; nothing in the small-ball mass. A better kink-mass model (Edgeworth density, L-O bounds, free models) cannot improve either chain; the targets are the variance transport (eq. cov-transport's kappa_3 terms, i.e. the F1 memory again) and the propagated mean.
claims.test: One run: recompute the chain's variance error against a fresh 1e8-input MC (variance floor 1.4e-4) and regress the injected error on (1/2) sigma phi eps_var; the attenuation-corrected explained fraction should rise from ~50% to >70% at layers 11-15 if the F6 lever is the whole injected error.

claims.claim: C5 (ii). C12 specialised to the commutative algebra (L^inf(R^n, N(0,I)), tau = E) with A = z_a, B = z_a + dz_a, P = 1_{z>0}, Q = 1_{z+dz>0}, |dz| <= h: ||P-Q||_2^2 = P(flip) = f(0) E|dz| + O(E dz^2) <= Q_A(h) = 2 f(0) h + O(h^2) [C11] <= tau(min(1, h^2/z^2)) = 2h^2 int_h^inf Q_A(t) t^{-3} dt = 4 f(0) h + O(h^2) [C12]. In the commutative case C11 is the sharper bound (1_{|z|<=h} <= min(1, h^2/z^2) pointwise), the exact flipped mass is half of C11 for sign-independent dz, and the C12 bound is loose by 4. The exponent: with the Holder form Q_A(t) <= C t^{alpha_s}, the mean shift obeys |dm - E[dz 1_{z>0}]| <= h P(flip) <= C' h^{1+alpha_s}, so for variance injection h ~ sqrt(eps) sigma the response is eps^{(1+alpha_s)/2}: the LINEARITY of F6 in eps is the statement alpha_s = 1 (continuous density); an atom at the kink (alpha_s = 0) would give sqrt(eps). The constant 1/2 of F6 is not obtainable from any L^2 bound (C12 gives 4 f(0) h^2 vs the exact (1/2) f(0) E dz^2).
claims.argument: Flip => z and z+dz have opposite signs => |z| <= |dz| <= h (one line). P(flip | dz = d) = |F(0) - F(-d)| = |d| f(0) + O(d^2). tau(min(1,h^2/z^2)) = int min(1, h^2/t^2) f(t) dt = f(0)(2h + 2h^2 int_h^inf t^{-2} dt) + O(h^2) = 4 f(0) h. The identity min(1,h^2/t^2) = int_h^inf 1_{|t|<=s} 2h^2 s^{-3} ds gives the Q_A integral. The mean-shift bound: relu(z+dz) - relu(z) - dz 1_{z>0} is supported on the flip event and bounded by |dz|. CHECKED: the our-data reader's gate-flip table (flips / two-sided small-ball event = 0.483-0.522, flips / rho_h(Gauss) = 0.467-0.525, exponent in h 0.976-1.029 at every layer); my Table B3 (exponent in eps 0.997-1.000, constant 0.997-1.000 of the exact 1/2); the companion-verify reader's C12 ratio 0.41-0.72 for commuting flips on GUE spectra (their factor-2 remark is the same computation).
claims.consequence_for_system: C12 adds nothing quantitative to F6 for diagonal (commuting) gates: the exact first-order law is sharper by a factor 8 and is what the chain already uses. Its one structural content transfers: the small-ball exponent alpha_s = 1 is why gate defects are first order (Hermite-degree-1-like) in a tilt and why the Euler-Stein kink content is a density, not a mass; nothing in the problem lives in the non-commutative regime where C12 would be the only tool.
claims.test: Done by the reader (flip fractions vs h) and here (Table B3). A decisive negative control would be a network with a bias that puts an atom at the kink; not relevant to the bias-free problem.

claims.claim: C6 (ii). The (1+tau)^{-1/2} decay of the kink content along Eldan's path: at layer 1 it is exact, E_{y~N(0,tau I)} f_a^{(y)}(0) = (f_a * phi_{2 tau})(0) = (2 pi (2 + 2 tau))^{-1/2} = (1+tau)^{-1/2} f_a(0), because m_a(y) = w_a . y ~ N(0, 2 tau) and sigma_a^2 = 2. The exponent -1/2 at large tau is the one-dimensional heat-kernel decay of the shift and is universal (any fluctuation density f, any small-ball exponent); the small-ball exponent alpha_s controls only the tau -> 0 behaviour ((f * phi_{s^2 tau})(0) ~ tau^{(alpha_s-1)/2}), so alpha_s = 1 is what makes the profile finite at tau = 0 and of the form (1+c tau)^{-1/2}. Measured on net 0 at ALL 16 layers (eldan_kink.py Table B1, N = 32768 per y, two y per tau): r1 = <f^{(y)}(0)>_a / <f^{(0)}(0)>_a = 0.855-0.893, 0.669-0.712, 0.432-0.470, 0.232-0.256 at tau = 0.25, 1, 4, 16 vs (1+tau)^{-1/2} = 0.894, 0.707, 0.447, 0.243; fitted (1+c tau)^{-q}: layer 0 c = 0.97, q = 0.503; layer 7 c = 1.52, q = 0.417; layer 15 c = 1.29, q = 0.459; the merge integral of the measured profile is a = 0.502, 0.496, 0.491. BUT the premise 'alpha ~ N(0, tau) at every layer by homogeneity' (sec_capacity) is false at depth: std_a(alpha^{(y)}) = 3.31, 3.49, 4.21, 6.07 at layer 15 (vs sqrt(tau) = 0.5, 1, 2, 4) and the fluctuation scale grows, <sigma^{(y)}>/<sigma^{(0)}> = 1.11, 1.32, 1.71, 2.23; the phi(alpha)-profile <sigma f> decays much more slowly (0.955, 0.910, 0.774, 0.526 at layer 15, a = 0.71). The (1+tau)^{-1/2} law holds for the absolute density f(0) = phi(alpha)/sigma, which is the quantity in the births and in the Hessian of the readout (C2), by a compensation between a steeper shift variance and the growth of sigma^{(y)}.
claims.status: PROVED (layer 1, and the large-tau exponent) + CHECKED (all layers, +-0.03)
claims.argument: Layer 1: z_1 = W_1(y + xi) is exactly N(W_1 y, W_1 W_1^T) with var 2 per neuron and (W_1 y)_a ~ N(0, 2 tau) over y, so the shifted density at 0 averages to the convolution value. Universality: for any density f with scale s and a Gaussian shift of variance v tau, (f * phi_{v tau})(0) -> (2 pi v tau)^{-1/2} as tau -> inf, independent of f; and (f * phi_{v tau})(0) at tau -> 0 is f(0) iff f is continuous at 0 (alpha_s = 1), ~ tau^{(alpha_s - 1)/2} otherwise. Deeper layers: measured, not proved; the homogeneity argument of sec_capacity only gives the scaling E(N(y, I)) = sqrt(1+tau) e(y/sqrt(1+tau)), not the N(0, tau) law of alpha, and Table B2 shows that law fails (the spread of alpha at tau = 0 is already 2.6-3 at depth). The identities.py check (D) confirms the Hermite-degree profiles E_{alpha~N(0,tau)} phi(alpha) He_d(alpha): (1+tau)^{-1/2} for d = 0 and (1+tau)^{-3/2} for d = 2, exactly.
claims.consequence_for_system: F5's midpoint a = 1/2 for the Gaussian closure is supported by the measured one-birth profile at every layer of the official network (a = 0.49-0.50), not only by the layer-1 computation; the mechanism is not the N(0, tau) law of alpha but the universal heat-kernel decay of the absolute kink density. The derivation of a from 'the Hermite degree of the kink content' must be done in absolute-density units; done in phi(alpha) units it would give a = 0.71 at depth, which is wrong.
claims.test: Done (Table B1). To close the proof gap at depth: measure the shift variance Var_y m_a(y) and sigma_a^{(y)} per layer and verify numerically that (f_a * phi_{Var m})(0) with the measured sigma^{(y)} reproduces r1; a 32768-input pass per (tau, y), 100 s each.

claims.claim: C7 (ii). Merge coefficient as a function of the decay profile: a = (1/2) int_0^inf (1+tau)^{-3/2} g(tau) dtau = 1/(2q+1) for g = (1+tau)^{-q}: 1/2 (one birth, q = 1/2), 1/3 (two births at distinct, weakly correlated neurons, q = 1), 1/4 (q = 3/2: three births, OR a single birth with Hermite-degree-2 kink content (alpha^2 - 1) phi(alpha), whose profile is exactly (1+tau)^{-3/2}); a same-neuron squared birth decays as (1+2 tau)^{-1/2} (a = 0.414 exactly at layer 0; measured profiles give a = 0.417, 0.379, 0.356 at layers 0, 7, 15). The organisers' chain's measured a = 0.255 (net 0) / 0.257 (net 1) corresponds to an equivalent pure power q = 1.45-1.46, i.e. to (1+tau)^{-3/2} (a = 0.250), NOT to two births (1/3) reduced by 'direction rotation' as sec_measure states. CONJECTURE: the kappa_3 chain's defect has Hermite-degree-2 kink content (the per-neuron kappa_4 readout term (alpha^2-1) phi sigma g4/24 that the radial kappa_4 does not carry, and the second y-derivatives of the kappa_3 slope term -g3 alpha phi sigma/6, both are He_2-type in alpha) and the 'rotation' at n = 256 is a small-size artefact; the two explanations predict different profiles.
claims.status: PROVED (the integrals and the Hermite profiles) + CONJECTURE (which profile the kappa_3 chain's defect has)
claims.argument: a_integral.py: a = 0.5000, 0.3333, 0.4142, 0.2500, 0.2000, 0.3660 for the six candidate profiles; a = 0.255 <=> q = 1.461. identities.py (D): E_{alpha~N(0,tau)} [phi He_2](alpha) / value at 0 = (1+tau)^{-3/2} to 4 digits (phi He_2 = phi'', convolution with phi_tau gives phi_{1+tau}''(0)). The measured same-neuron squared profile r2same (Table B1) is (1+2 tau)^{-1/2} at layer 0 (0.814/0.583/0.339/0.176 vs 0.816/0.577/0.333/0.174) and steeper at depth (0.781/0.504/0.262/0.099 at layer 15, fit (1+1.84 tau)^{-0.65}). The note's rotation explanation rests on a single n = 256, L = 4 Gaussian-closure measurement (g = 0.91, 0.56, 0.15, 0.02 vs |E delta|/|delta(0)| = 0.96, 0.73, 0.46, 0.28); no profile of the kappa_3 chain's defect has been measured at any size.
claims.consequence_for_system: If the He_2 explanation is right, a = 1/4 is a derived constant for the kappa_3 chain with no rotation correction, the defect's tau-profile is (1+tau)^{-3/2}, and the Euler-Stein integral is dominated by tau < 2 (84% of the weight), which lowers the cost of any path-sampled correction; if the two-births-plus-rotation explanation is right, the correction constant is size-dependent. The deciding measurement for task #13 (short-memory chains) depends on which: a window-1 chain whose dropped memory is a kappa_3 slope term would again have q = 3/2 content.
claims.test: Profile of the kprop3 defect on a small network (n = 256, L = 4, as in scripts/defect_profile.py but with the organisers' chain): delta(y) by 2n+1 = 513 chain runs per y, at tau = 0.25, 1, 4, 16 with 2 y each (about 4000 small-chain runs). Discriminator: g(1) = 0.354 and g(4) = 0.089 for (1+tau)^{-3/2} versus g(1) = 0.5 x rotation and g(4) = 0.2 x rotation for two births; the |E delta|/|delta(0)| norm profile separates rotation from decay.

claims.claim: C8 (iii). There is no arithmetic structure: the inverse Littlewood-Offord theory (Tao-Vu, Nguyen-Vu, Rudelson-Vershynin LCD, Theorem 4.2 of the survey: P(|<X,v>| <= eps) <= C eps + e^{-c alpha n} when D_alpha(v) > c/eps) does not apply and has nothing to say, because its premise is independent discrete summands and its conclusion (v near a generalized arithmetic progression) describes an excess concentration rho_eps >> eps that never occurs here. For the pre-activation z_a = sum_r w_ar h_r the only discrete objects, the gates, are deterministic functions of the continuous input, so conditionally on all gate patterns z_a is a nonzero linear functional of a cone-truncated Gaussian; the concentration function is exactly rho_eps = 2 f_a(0) eps (1 + O(eps)) with no additive floor, and 'LCD = infinity' in the Esseen sense: the characteristic function psi_a(theta) decays like a Gaussian. CHECKED: |psi_a(theta)| averaged over neurons at theta sigma = 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 2.5, 3 is 0.8826, 0.608, 0.328, 0.139-0.141, 0.047-0.048, 0.013-0.014 at layers 2-14 vs Gaussian 0.8825, 0.6065, 0.3247, 0.1353, 0.0439, 0.0111 and Edgeworth (g3, g4) 0.8826, 0.608, 0.327-0.329, 0.137-0.142, 0.045-0.050, 0.012-0.014; the rms of psi_emp - psi_Edg is 0.0000-0.0056, at the 1/sqrt(N) = 0.0055 floor at theta sigma = 3 (no plateau, no lattice peaks); the reader's small-ball ratios are 1.000-1.003 down to h = 0.003 sigma.
claims.status: PROVED (structure) + CHECKED (characteristic function and small-ball ratios)
claims.argument: Structure as in C1. Esseen's inequality rho_eps(X) <= C eps int_{|theta| <= 1/eps} |psi_X(theta)| dtheta makes the concentration function a functional of |psi| up to frequency 1/eps; the LCD of a coefficient vector is exactly the frequency scale at which |psi| of a Rademacher sum stops decaying (Rudelson-Vershynin's (54): |E exp(i<u,Y>)| <= exp(-c inf_r ||r v||_T^2)); for a law whose psi decays like exp(-theta^2 sigma^2/2) times an Edgeworth polynomial, that scale is infinite and rho_eps = 2 f(0) eps exactly to O(eps^2). The survey itself (lines 1131-1132) calls the continuous case 'vastly easier' for this reason. Table B4 of eldan_kink.log (N = 32768, phases removed by exp(-i theta alpha)).
claims.consequence_for_system: No estimate of Littlewood-Offord type (classical, inverse, typical, LCD, approximate negative correlation) bears on F4-F6: the gate statistics are governed by a smooth density whose Gaussian surrogate is right to 1e-3 and whose Edgeworth corrections are the kappa_3, kappa_4 terms the chain already carries. The F4 obstruction (zero mean of sketches on trilinear forms) is a parity fact, not an anti-concentration failure.
claims.test: Done (Table B4, reader's Table A1). A negative control that would reveal arithmetic structure if it existed: the same characteristic-function scan at theta sigma = 4-6 with N = 1e6 inputs (floor 1e-3; Gaussian value 3e-4 to 1e-8) — any plateau above the Edgeworth curve would be a lattice signature; I predict none.

claims.claim: C9 (iii). The analogue of the least common denominator is not arithmetic but dimensional: the parameter that controls the deviation of the gate statistics from their Gaussian value is the standardized cumulant vector (g3, g4) of the hub sum, and at depth it is carried by a ~100-dimensional collective subspace of the previous layer, not by independent summands and not by a single collective mode. Measured (skew_rank.py, skew_collective.py): (a) the independent-summand (Berry-Esseen) prediction g3_ind,a = sum_r w_ar^3 kappa_3(h_r)/sigma_a^3 has rms 0.006 -> 0.002 (layers 1 -> 15), explains the skewness at layer 1 (corr 0.78, slope 1.2) and nothing at depth (corr 0.15, slope 7.4 at layer 15 where rms g3 = 0.112); (b) the top covariance mode alone, sign(u_a) p_a^{3/2} g3(c) with p_a = lambda_1 u_a^2/var_a, gives the right PATTERN at depth (corr 0.78 at layer 15, 0.73 at layer 11) but only 1/5.7 of the magnitude (g3(c) = 0.22, lambda_1/tr C = 0.096, cos(mean, u_1) = 0.978); (c) restricting kappa_3(z_a) to the top-K eigen-subspace of the pre-activation covariance recovers, at layer 15, corr 0.78 / 0.93 / 0.98 and 14% / 45% / 92% of the rms for K = 1 / 16 / 128 (layer 11: 0.73 / 0.91 / 0.96; layer 7: 0.69 / 0.86 / 0.92; layer 3: 0.35 / 0.64 / 0.77, needing K > 128). The He-row delocalisation (w_ar ~ N(0, 2/n)) is the analogue of the flatness condition ||v||_inf <= n^{-c} (Lemma 7.5 of Sah-Sahasrabudhe-Sawhney) and is what makes the independent part O(n^{-1/2}) and realization-specific with zero ensemble mean; the collective structure is F7 seen from the kink, and its rank ~10^2 is F3's rank obstruction (99%-rank > 256 of the cocycle) seen from the kink.
claims.status: CHECKED (the independent-summand formula and the subspace restriction are exact identities; the dimension counts are measurements on net 0)
claims.argument: kappa_3(z_a) = sum_{ijk} w_ai w_aj w_ak kappa_3(h_i, h_j, h_k) exactly; the diagonal i = j = k part is g3_ind (with kappa_3(h_r) from the Gaussian law of z_r at the true (m, sigma)); the top-K restriction is sum_{ijk <= K} U_ai U_aj U_ak kappa_3(c_i, c_j, c_k) with c = U^T z, computed from a 16384-input MC (third-moment tensor up to 128^3). The CP/hub structure of F1 is this tensor written as rank-2n blocks per birth; the skewness at the kink needs the same object. The collective-mode share lambda_1/tr of the CENTRED covariance is 0.006 (layer 1) -> 0.096 (layer 15); F7's 37-48% refers to the uncentred second moment (mean-aligned).
claims.consequence_for_system: The 'structure' that an inverse theorem would detect is low-dimensional only in the weak sense of ~10^2 directions out of 1024, growing toward full rank at early layers; a rank-K readout of the kink statistics with K ~ 10 captures the sign pattern but < 40% of the magnitude, which is the same conclusion as F3's subspace readouts (crossover r ~ n^{2/3} = 101). There is no cheap arithmetic or low-rank summary of the gate statistics; the kink does not offer a route around the n^3 memory.
claims.test: Done at N = 16384. Decisive extension: the same top-K restriction for kappa_3 of the POST-activation h at the source layer (the births) and its transport through one layer, checking that the explained fraction after transport equals the explained fraction of the hub readout at rank K (predicted ~ legE(K)^3 by the free-derandomization reader); one MC pass plus K^3 tensors, under 10 minutes.

verdict: Lens 1 settles three things and leaves one open. (i) PROVED+CHECKED: the kink density phi(alpha)/sigma is the h->0 small-ball limit of an absolutely continuous law with exponent exactly 1, and the true value equals the Gaussian surrogate's to 1-3e-3 when (m, sigma) are true; but the closure error is NOT the kink mass. At exact moments the Gaussian closure's one-step error is the kappa_3-weighted slope of the surrogate density at the kink, -kappa_3 f_G'(0)/6 (5-6e-4 rms per layer, slope 0.92 vs the 1e9-sample truth), and for the organisers' chain the per-layer error at depth is 85% propagated mean error and the rest the F6 variance lever on a ~2e-3 variance deficit (injected 1.4e-5 -> 5.6e-5 rms against a 2.7e-5 truth floor, uncorrelated with the kappa_3 and kappa_4 shape terms). The hypothesis 'kink mass dominates the closure error' is REFUTED; the kink mass enters only as the propagation coefficient (sensitivity law exact to 0.3% with the empirical density, exponent 1.000 in eps). (ii) C12 in the commutative setting collapses to C11 and both are loose (factor 2 and 4) against the exact first-order law P(flip) = f(0) E|dz|; its only transferable content is that the small-ball exponent alpha_s = 1 is the exponent of the sensitivity law (dm ~ eps^{(1+alpha_s)/2}) and the reason the Euler-Stein kink content is a density. The (1+tau)^{-1/2} profile is exact at layer 1, universal at large tau (1-D heat kernel, independent of the law), and CHECKED at all 16 layers of net 0 for the absolute kink density (a = 0.49-0.50), although the note's premise alpha ~ N(0, tau) fails at depth and the phi(alpha)-profile would give a = 0.71: the derivation of merge coefficients must be done in absolute-density units. The organisers' chain's a = 0.255-0.257 corresponds to a (1+tau)^{-3/2} profile (a = 1/4; q = 1.46), i.e. Hermite-degree-2 kink content, not 'two births reduced by rotation' (1/3); which is right is OPEN and decided by one small-network profile measurement (about 4000 n=256 chain runs). (iii) PROVED: no arithmetic structure exists (gates are functions of the continuous input; rho_eps = 2 f(0) eps exactly to O(eps^2); characteristic function Gaussian-with-Edgeworth to the 1/sqrt(N) floor); the LCD's analogue is dimensional: the gate statistics' non-Gaussianity at depth is carried by a ~100-dimensional collective subspace (top mode: right pattern, 1/5.7 of the magnitude; K = 128 recovers 92% at layer 15, less at early layers), with the independent (Berry-Esseen, n^{-1/2}, zero-mean) part negligible beyond layer 3. Net for the system: nothing from the concentration-function literature improves either chain; the errors at the kink are the variance transport and the propagated mean (F6, F1), and the kink statistics exhibit the same rank-10^2 structure as F3. The one actionable item is the defect-profile measurement that fixes whether a = 1/4 is a derived constant for first-order chains.
